questions.question:
Germs that infect the respiratory system are frequently spread through
I. mucus
II. air pollution
III. coughs
questions.explanation: Respiratory germs spread through mucus (from sneezing/coughing), air pollution (carrying germs in dust/droplets), and coughs (releasing germs into the air). All three contribute to spread.

questions.question: Which of the following food substances would produce a red precipitate when heated with Millon's reagent?
questions.explanation: Millon's reagent tests for proteins. It produces a red precipitate when heated with protein-containing foods. Groundnuts are rich in protein, while the others are primarily carbohydrate or sugar-rich.

questions.question: An organism that lives on decaying organic matter, contaminates human food, feeds on rotten fruits and transfers germs is most likely a
questions.explanation: Houseflies feed on decaying matter and rotten fruits, then land on human food, transferring germs from their legs and body to the food.

questions.question: A fruit with sour taste is most likely to have a pH that is
questions.explanation: Sour-tasting substances are acidic. Acids have a pH less than 7. A pH of 7 is neutral, greater than 7 is alkaline, and 14 is strongly alkaline.

questions.question:
Which of the following energy sources is/are environmentally friendly?
I. Wind
II. Hydro
III. Biomass
questions.explanation: Wind, hydro (water), and biomass are all renewable energy sources that produce less pollution compared to fossil fuels. They are considered environmentally friendly.

questions.question: Which of the following activities does not relate to the principles of pressure in the daily lives of humans?
options: A. Drinking straw in use by people at a party
B. Pumping air into car tyres
C. Filling of balloons with air
D. A person jerking forward when a speeding car suddenly stops
questions.explanation: A person jerking forward when a car stops is due to inertia (Newton's first law), not pressure. The other options all involve air pressure — straws, tyres, and balloons all use pressure principles.

questions.question: The rise in heat waves and floods globally may be due to the effect of
questions.explanation: Climate change is the broader phenomenon causing increased heat waves, floods, and extreme weather. Greenhouse gases cause climate change, but the overall effect described is climate change.

questions.question: The following soil qualities are important for crop production except
questions.explanation: High salinity (too much salt) is harmful to crops — it damages roots and reduces water uptake. Nutrient availability, oxygen, and water-holding capacity are all beneficial for crop growth.

questions.question: A rod appears bent when immersed in water. Which property of light is demonstrated?
questions.explanation: Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium to another. When light travels from water to air, it bends, making the rod appear bent.

questions.question: The following factors hinder vegetable production in Ghana except
options: A. high cost of agricultural chemicals
B. lack of market for farm produce
questions.explanation: Availability of sunlight helps vegetable production, it does not hinder it. High cost of chemicals, lack of market, and irregular rainfall are all challenges facing vegetable farmers in Ghana.

questions.question: Which of the following types of manure is suitable for a vegetable garden?
questions.explanation: Cow dung is a safe and effective organic manure for vegetable gardens. Dog waste and human excreta can contain harmful pathogens that may contaminate food crops.

questions.question: An example of a monogastric animal is
questions.explanation: A monogastric animal has one stomach. Rabbits are monogastric. Cattle, goats, and sheep are ruminants — they have four stomach chambers.

questions.question:
Which of the following insect(s) show(s) the egg, nymph and adult stages in its life cycle?
I. Grasshopper
II. Housefly
III. Mosquito
questions.explanation: The grasshopper undergoes incomplete metamorphosis: egg → nymph → adult. Houseflies and mosquitoes undergo complete metamorphosis: egg → larva → pupa → adult.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best explains the term ecosystem? It is
options: A. a group of organisms of the same species that live in the same place at the same time
B. a group of populations living in the same area at the same time
C. the part of the earth's environment where life exists
D. a community of living and non-living things interacting with each other
questions.explanation: An ecosystem includes both living (biotic) and non-living (abiotic) components interacting together in an area. Option A describes a population, B describes a community.

questions.question:
The characteristics of a fertile soil include good
I. aeration
II. texture
III. water-holding capacity
questions.explanation: Fertile soil has good aeration (air spaces for roots), good texture (mixture of sand, silt, clay), and good water-holding capacity. All three are important for healthy plant growth.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases can be classified as a viral disease?
questions.explanation: H1N1 (swine flu) is caused by a virus. Candidiasis and ringworm are fungal infections. Meningitis can be caused by bacteria, viruses, or fungi.

questions.question: The chemical formula of iron (II) sulphide is
questions.explanation: Iron (II) means iron has a charge of +2. Sulphur forms a sulphide ion with charge -2. To balance: one Fe²⁺ combines with one S²⁻, giving FeS.

questions.question: A book is at rest on a table. The net force acting on the book could be described as one that
questions.explanation: When an object is at rest, the forces on it are balanced. The weight of the book is balanced by the upward normal force from the table. Balanced forces result in no movement.

questions.question: Which of the following Ghanaian scientists is known for promoting Mathematics and Physics?
questions.explanation: Prof. Francis Allotey was a renowned Ghanaian physicist known for the 'Allotey Formalism' in physics. He promoted mathematics and physics education in Ghana.

questions.question: Which of the following heart conditions in humans is caused by plaque deposits in the arteries?
questions.explanation: Atherosclerosis is the buildup of fatty plaques in artery walls, narrowing the arteries. This can lead to heart attack or stroke, but the condition itself is atherosclerosis.

questions.question: A mango of mass 1.5 kg hangs 20 m on top of a mango tree. Determine the value of the kinetic energy attained just before it hits the ground. [g = 10 ms⁻²]
questions.explanation: At the top, the mango has potential energy = mgh = 1.5 × 10 × 20 = 300 J. Just before hitting the ground, all this potential energy converts to kinetic energy = 300 J.

questions.question: A grassland ecosystem that consists of snakes, toads and grasshoppers is most likely to produce a food chain of
questions.explanation: A food chain starts with a producer (grass), then primary consumer (grasshopper eats grass), secondary consumer (toad eats grasshopper), and tertiary consumer (snake eats toad).

questions.question: The first step in the digestion of fats in the body is that
options: A. bile breaks down the fat in the gall bladder
B. bile breaks down the fat in the duodenum
C. lipase breaks down the fat in the pancreas
D. lipase breaks down the fat in the ileum
questions.explanation: Bile is produced in the liver and stored in the gall bladder. It is released into the duodenum where it emulsifies (breaks down) fats into smaller droplets.

questions.question: Which of the following waste disposal practices is best for plastic disposal?
questions.explanation: Recycling is the best option for plastics. Burning releases toxic fumes, composting only works for organic waste, and incineration can release harmful chemicals.

questions.question: A patient has been diagnosed with hypertension. Which of the following readings is most likely the patient's blood pressure?
questions.explanation: Normal blood pressure is about 120/80. Hypertension (high blood pressure) is diagnosed when readings are consistently 140/90 or higher.

questions.question:
Which of the following substances are major components of human blood?
I. Hormones
II. Platelets
III. Plasma
IV. White blood cells
options: D. II, III and IV only
questions.explanation: Blood is made up of platelets (help clotting), plasma (liquid part), and white blood cells (fight infection). Hormones are chemicals carried by blood but are not a major component.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is prokaryotic?
questions.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotic — they have no membrane-bound nucleus. Earthworms, fungi, and plants are all eukaryotic (they have a true nucleus).

questions.question: An example of a communicable disease is
questions.explanation: Hepatitis is a viral infection that spreads from person to person. Asthma, diabetes, and hypertension are non-communicable — they cannot be passed from one person to another.

questions.question: The S.I unit of energy is represented as
questions.explanation: The SI unit of energy is the Joule. When written as a symbol, it should be capital 'J' (named after a person). The word 'Joule' is the name, 'J' is the symbol.

questions.question: A breeding female pig is called a
questions.explanation: A sow is an adult female pig that has already given birth. A gilt is a young female pig that has not yet borne young. Doe is for rabbits, heifer for cattle.

questions.question: Which of the following associations between two organisms is always beneficial to both?
questions.explanation: Mutualism is a relationship where both organisms benefit. Commensalism benefits one without affecting the other. Saprophytism involves feeding on dead matter.

questions.question: To stop the spread of a disease caused by a dirty environment, one must
questions.explanation: Diseases caused by dirty environments spread through contact with contaminated surfaces, water, or food. Personal hygiene (washing hands, keeping clean) breaks this chain of transmission.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best explains why gases are more compressible than solids?
options: A. Particles in gases are smaller than in solids
B. Gases have fixed volume but solids do not
C. Particles in solids have definite shape but gases have no definite shape
D. Particles in gases have wider intermolecular spaces as compared to solids
questions.explanation: Gas particles are far apart with wide spaces between them, so they can be pushed closer together (compressed). Solid particles are closely packed with very little space between them.

questions.question: Which of the following substances has a definite shape?
questions.explanation: A stone is a solid — it has both definite shape and definite volume. Air is a gas, kerosene and water are liquids — they do not have definite shapes.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best explains livestock feed?
options: A. Food grown or developed for livestock
B. Balanced diet provided to animals
C. Breast milk served to a calf
D. Grass that is used to feed livestock
questions.explanation: Livestock feed refers to any food grown or developed specifically for feeding farm animals. It includes concentrates, forages, and compounded feeds — not just grass or milk.

questions.question: Combination of science, technology and innovation is needed in Ghana because it
options: A. equips students to travel abroad and work
B. makes students develop interest in science, technology and innovation
C. makes students understand their environment better
questions.explanation: The main reason Ghana needs science, technology and innovation is to promote national development — improving agriculture, health, industry, and infrastructure.

questions.question: Charles Darwin is famous for
options: B. his work on the origin of the universe
C. his work in the field of physics
D. his theory of natural selection
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin is famous for his theory of natural selection, which explains how species evolve over time. He published this idea in 'On the Origin of Species' (1859).

questions.question: Which of the following statements accurately explains the positions of calcium and magnesium in the periodic table? They all have the same
questions.explanation: Calcium and magnesium are both in Group 2 of the periodic table. Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons (outer shell electrons).

questions.question: An animal feed made up of high fibre is most likely to contain
questions.explanation: Silage is fermented plant material (grass, maize, etc.) that is high in fibre. It is commonly used as feed for ruminant animals like cattle and goats.

questions.question: The term used to describe a rabbit giving birth is
questions.explanation: Kindling is the term for a rabbit giving birth. Culling is removing unwanted animals, dubbing is cutting parts of animals, and weaning is stopping milk feeding.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of living things?
questions.explanation: Respiration is a key characteristic of all living things — they take in oxygen and release energy from food. Not all living things are stationary, green, or microscopic.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a renewable energy source?
questions.explanation: Petroleum (oil) is a fossil fuel — it takes millions of years to form and cannot be replaced once used. Solar, wind, and hydro are renewable because they replenish naturally.

questions.question: The process by which green plants make their own food is called
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process where green plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to make glucose (food) and oxygen.

questions.question: Which organ in the human body is responsible for pumping blood?
questions.explanation: The heart is a muscular organ that pumps blood throughout the body through the blood vessels. It beats about 100,000 times per day.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a simple machine?
questions.explanation: A lever is a simple machine — a basic device that makes work easier by changing the direction or magnitude of a force. Computers, TVs, and refrigerators are complex machines.

questions.question: Which of the following is a sexually transmitted infection?
questions.explanation: Syphilis is a sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by bacteria. Malaria is transmitted by mosquitoes, cholera and typhoid are waterborne diseases.

questions.question: The deforestation of forests leads to
options: D. more oxygen in the air
questions.explanation: Removing trees exposes soil to rain and wind, causing soil erosion. Trees also absorb carbon dioxide and produce oxygen — deforestation reduces oxygen and increases CO₂.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to test for the presence of starch?
questions.explanation: Iodine solution turns blue-black in the presence of starch. Benedict's solution tests for reducing sugars, litmus paper tests for acids and bases.

questions.question: Which of the following animals is a herbivore?
questions.explanation: A herbivore feeds only on plants. The grasshopper eats grass and leaves. Lions, dogs, and eagles are carnivores — they eat meat.

questions.question: The colour of the heartwood in a tree trunk is usually
questions.explanation: Heartwood is the older, central part of a tree trunk. It is darker than sapwood because it is filled with resins and tannins that make it harder and more durable.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of blood?
questions.explanation: Neurons are nerve cells found in the brain and nerves, not in blood. Blood contains red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, and plasma.

questions.question: Which of the following is a consequence of drug abuse?
questions.explanation: Drug abuse damages organs, especially the liver which filters drugs from the blood. It also causes mental health problems, addiction, and can be fatal.

questions.question: Which layer of the atmosphere contains the ozone layer?
questions.explanation: The ozone layer is in the stratosphere, about 15-35 km above the Earth. It absorbs harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to measure temperature?
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature. A barometer measures atmospheric pressure, a hygrometer measures humidity, and a rain gauge measures rainfall.

questions.question: Which of the following is a product of photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: During photosynthesis, plants take in carbon dioxide and water, and produce glucose (food) and oxygen. The oxygen is released into the air.

questions.question: The boiling point of pure water at standard atmospheric pressure is
questions.explanation: Pure water boils at 100°C at standard atmospheric pressure (1 atmosphere). At this temperature, water changes from liquid to gas (steam).

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a decomposer?
questions.explanation: Mushrooms (fungi) are decomposers — they break down dead organic matter into simpler substances. Grass is a producer, rabbits and eagles are consumers.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Good conductors of electricity (like metals) have free electrons that can move easily, allowing electric current to flow through them.

questions.question: The upward force that acts on an object immersed in a fluid is called
questions.explanation: Buoyancy is the upward force exerted by a fluid on an object immersed in it. It is why objects float — the buoyant force opposes the weight of the object.

questions.question: Which of the following is the main function of the root in a plant?
options: B. Absorption of water and minerals
questions.explanation: The main function of roots is to absorb water and dissolved minerals from the soil. Roots also anchor the plant firmly in the ground.

questions.question: Which of the following is a non-renewable resource?
questions.explanation: Natural gas is a fossil fuel formed over millions of years — once used, it cannot be replaced within a human lifetime. Solar, wind, and water are renewable.

questions.question: The process by which water vapour changes into liquid water is called
questions.explanation: Condensation is when water vapour (gas) cools and turns into liquid water. This is how clouds form — water vapour in the air cools and condenses into tiny droplets.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest organ in the human body?
questions.explanation: The skin is the largest organ in the human body. It covers the entire body, protects against infection, regulates temperature, and senses touch.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a mixture?
questions.explanation: Air is a mixture of gases — mainly nitrogen (78%) and oxygen (21%), with small amounts of other gases. Pure water, salt, and iron are pure substances.

questions.question: The deficiency of Vitamin C in the body causes
questions.explanation: Scurvy is caused by Vitamin C deficiency — it leads to bleeding gums, weakness, and slow wound healing. Rickets is Vitamin D, Beriberi is Vitamin B1, night blindness is Vitamin A.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a method of separating mixtures?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is how plants make food, not a separation method. Filtration, distillation, and evaporation are all techniques used to separate mixtures.

questions.question: Which of the following planets is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars is called the Red Planet because iron oxide (rust) on its surface gives it a reddish appearance. It is the fourth planet from the Sun.

questions.question: The type of energy possessed by a moving object is
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion. Any object that is moving has kinetic energy. The faster it moves, the more kinetic energy it has.

questions.question: Which of the following is an effect of deforestation?
questions.explanation: Deforestation removes trees that hold soil in place, leading to soil erosion. It also reduces biodiversity, decreases rainfall, and increases carbon dioxide in the air.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct arrangement of the electromagnetic spectrum in order of increasing frequency?
options: A. Radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays
B. Gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible light, infrared, microwaves, radio waves
C. Visible light, infrared, microwaves, radio waves, gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet
D. Radio waves, visible light, microwaves, infrared, gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet
questions.explanation: The electromagnetic spectrum from lowest to highest frequency is: radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays.

questions.question: An object is placed in front of a plane mirror. The image formed is
questions.explanation: A plane mirror forms a virtual image that is upright (not upside down) and the same size as the object. The image appears behind the mirror.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of sound waves?
options: A. They can travel through a vacuum
C. They need a medium to travel
D. They travel faster than light
questions.explanation: Sound waves are mechanical waves — they need a medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel. They cannot travel through a vacuum (empty space).

questions.question: The organ that filters blood in the human body is the
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter blood to remove waste products and excess water, producing urine. They filter about 180 litres of blood daily.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a renewable energy source?
questions.explanation: Solar energy comes from the sun and is constantly replenished — it is renewable. Coal, natural gas, and petroleum are fossil fuels that take millions of years to form.

questions.question: Which of the following is a function of the skeleton in the human body?
options: C. Production of blood cells only
questions.explanation: The skeleton protects internal organs — the skull protects the brain, the ribcage protects the heart and lungs, and the spine protects the spinal cord.

questions.question: The chemical symbol for water is
questions.explanation: Water is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom, giving it the chemical formula H₂O.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of soil?
questions.explanation: There is no such thing as gaseous soil. Sandy, clayey, and loamy are the three main types of soil based on particle size and composition.

questions.question: Which of the following activities can lead to water pollution?
questions.explanation: Dumping waste into rivers introduces harmful chemicals and bacteria into the water, making it unsafe for drinking, fishing, and other uses.

questions.question: The process by which a liquid changes into a gas at temperatures below its boiling point is called
questions.explanation: Evaporation happens at any temperature — the surface molecules of a liquid gain enough energy to escape as gas. Boiling happens at a specific temperature throughout the liquid.

questions.question: Which of the following is the main source of energy for the Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun is the main source of energy for the Earth. It provides light and heat energy that drives weather, photosynthesis, and life on Earth.
